rich_summary: The passage closes the cosmological discourse describing the sizes of celestial bodies such as the Sun and Moon and the role of Rahu in eclipses, asserting that these measurements come from scriptural science. It then shifts abruptly to the opening of the Bhagavat‑Gita Parva within the Mahabharata war narrative. Sanjaya arrives at Dhritarashtra’s court and reports the devastating news that Bhishma—the invincible grandsire and pillar of the Kaurava army—has fallen, lying on a bed of arrows after being brought down through Sikhandin’s presence in battle. Dhritarashtra responds with shock and grief, recounting Bhishma’s unmatched valor and moral stature while questioning how such a warrior could be defeated. His lament underscores the tragic inevitability of fate and the catastrophic turning point for the Kaurava cause.

highlight_spans.why: Opens the cosmological measurements that frame the universe according to the Shastras.
The pivotal announcement that Bhishma has been slain, triggering the emotional and narrative shift.
Evokes the iconic image of Bhishma lying on a bed of arrows, one of the Mahabharata’s most memorable scenes.
Dhritarashtra’s grief-filled reflection on Bhishma’s greatness highlights the tragic weight of the loss.
Philosophical reflection that even weapons, courage, or wisdom cannot overcome Time, reinforcing the epic’s theme of destiny.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma lying on a vast bed of arrows at sunset on the battlefield while warriors from both sides look on in awe and grief.
Sanjaya standing in Dhritarashtra’s dark court, delivering the devastating news while the blind king sits frozen in shock.
Bhishma in battle like a storm of arrows, his bow roaring like thunder as terrified soldiers scatter before him.
